suggestions.text: Patient is a 67-year-old male admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease stage 3, hyperkalemia, and acute glycemic instability. Known history includes type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a penicillin allergy resulting in rash. Vital signs and laboratory findings on admission show ongoing fever, elevated inflammatory markers, and worsening renal function.
Patient's baseline serum creatinine prior to admission
Outpatient blood pressure and glycemic control logs
Sputum culture and sensitivity results
What was the patient's baseline renal function prior to this admission?
Has the patient experienced any other allergic reactions or side effects from antibiotics in the past?

Best Possible Medication History includes home use of metformin, amlodipine, and OTC ibuprofen. Reconciliation reveals amlodipine was omitted from admission orders without explicit documentation, while ibuprofen and metformin continue inpatient despite acute kidney injury. Every new inpatient medication order has an identified indication.
